item.title: Manhattan University Launches Minor in Artificial Intelligence
item.description:
# Manhattan University Launches Minor in Artificial Intelligence Starting Fall 2026, Manhattan University is launching a new minor program in Artificial Intelligence.
Image
![AI or Artificial intelligence concept. Businessman using computer use ai to help business and used in daily life, Digital Transformation, Internet of Things, Artificial intelligence brain,](https://manhattan.edu/sites/default/files/styles/4_3_327w/public/media/2026-07/ai-minor-3000x2000.jpg?h=c6980913&itok=lYbPpHEH)
RIVERDALE, N.Y. — Manhattan University will launch a [minor in artificial intelligence](https://manhattan.edu/academics/programs/ai-minor) in fall 2026, giving students across every discipline structured instruction in how intelligent systems work and how to apply them responsibly.
The new minor draws on the combined strengths of all three of the University's schools, the Kakos School of Arts and Sciences, the O'Malley School of Business and the School of Engineering, and builds on established programs in computer science, computer information systems, business analytics, and electrical and computer engineering.
"Artificial intelligence touches every discipline, and our students deserve more than a surface-level familiarity with it," said Bridget Chalk, Ph.D., provost of Manhattan University. "This minor gives students in any major, from business to engineering to the liberal arts, a genuine understanding of how AI works and how to use it responsibly in their fields."
Open to students in every major across the University, the minor was developed jointly by faculty in computer science, computer information systems, business analytics, accounting, law, and electrical, computer and mechanical engineering. It provides structured, interdisciplinary instruction in AI fundamentals: how intelligent systems work, what their limitations are and how to apply them responsibly.
Students choose from a core of upper-level courses in areas including machine learning, data mining, deep learning and generative AI, trustworthy AI, image processing, and AI applications in business and engineering design.
Consistent with the University's Lasallian mission, the minor also challenges students to weigh the ethical and societal implications of artificial intelligence, asking not only what intelligent systems can do, but what they should do.
For more information, visit manhattan.edu/AI.
**Media Contact:**
Robert Cole
Executive Director of Marketing
Manhattan University

item.title: Great Valley adds research-focused master's to artificial intelligence programs
item.description:
# Great Valley adds research-focused master's to artificial intelligence programs ## New research-intensive master of science degree prepares students for research careers in industry and academia and for doctoral study MALVERN, Pa. — Penn State Great Valley will offer a [master of science in artificial intelligence](https://greatvalley.psu.edu/academics/masters-degrees/master-science-artificial-intelligence) (AI), beginning in fall 2026.
“The M.S. in artificial intelligence addresses the growing need for professionals who can conduct original research and develop new AI methods,” said Youakim Badr, professor-in-charge of the artificial intelligence program.
## Great Valley’s AI graduate programs The new M.S. in artificial intelligence expands Great Valley’s portfolio by providing a research-oriented pathway for students who want to develop new AI methods, contribute original knowledge to the field or prepare for doctoral study.
In contrast with Great Valley’s [master of artificial intelligence](https://greatvalley.psu.edu/academics/masters-degrees/master-artificial-intelligence), which is oriented toward professional practice, this research-oriented M.S. program emphasizes theoretical foundations, mathematical modeling, algorithm development and empirical research.
The master of artificial intelligence, highly ranked by U.S. News and World Report, has two options: AI engineering, for programmers who want to design these systems, or the [applied and generative AI option](https://www.worldcampus.psu.edu/degrees-and-certificates/penn-state-online-artificial-intelligence-applied-and-generative-ai-masters-degree), offered only online, which harnesses low- or no-code AI tools for business innovation and transformation.
Great Valley’s new [MBA in AI program](https://greatvalley.psu.edu/academics/masters-degrees/business-artificial-intelligence/), also launching in fall 2026, equips students with expertise in both AI and business, preparing them to redesign organizational workflows and build AI-powered enterprises.
